Maintenance & Warranties A couple of weeks ago, our home A/C went out... As it is already 92° here in Tooele Utah, you can see that it is a problem! Luckily our realtor/landlady who we rented from for two years before we purchased our new home recommended that we ask the seller to buy a Home Warranty for us as a part of the sale. We added $75 to upgrade our package and we have definitely used it! We chose Home Warranty of America, https://www.hwahomewarranty.com/ , and we have been VERY satisfied. We will be renewing our warranty this September. So, when our A/C went out, we called HWA (Home Warranty of America) and they sent out a repairman. He did what he could with the signs that the A/C was presenting while he was here. He also helped us locate our HVAC filter, as we hadn't been able to locate it. The previous owners had put the filter in backwards and on top of that, it was overdue for replacing. I had always heard that you should replace filters yearly, but both my parents and the HVAC repairman said that it should be done every month to three months! We were WAY overdue... The repair-person got everything running appropriately for the moment, but the A/C stopped again a few hours after he left, so another repair-person will be coming tomorrow. If the A/C can't be fixed, the Warranty company will pay up to $5,000 towards a new A/C! Hopefully it won't come to that, but it is good to know. Had I added a Maintenance Schedule to my Google Calendar, this might never have happened... Here is a GREAT Scheduler that I found that can be added to your Google Calender to keep you up-to-date on your Home Maintenance: https://www.homelight.com/blog/home-maintenance-schedule/ In addition to Home Maintenance, Vehicle Maintenance is just as important! Some time last fall-winter I got a small chip in my front windshield. We're tight on money and living in an area that we are still learning, so I wasn't automatically aware of where I should take my car for windshield care... That led to me procrastinating. BIG Mistake! It only cost me $45 dollars to get the chip sealed and if I would have done that when I first noticed the chip, the chip wouldn't have grown larger. Now, though it has been sealed, there is a much larger possibility that the chip will continue to expand. So... Here is a Car Maintenance app that you can use for free: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=mrigapps.andriod.fuelcons&hl=en_US And here is a List for AAA for what needs to be maintained and how often that you can coordinate with the app linked above: https://www.aaa.com/autorepair/articles/time-stamped-car-maintenance-checklist Don't be like me, prevent the more costly repairs by maintaining your home and vehicles!

It assumed the functions of the AEC not assumed by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission . The agency was created as part of the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974 , which was passed on October 11, 1974, in the wake of the 1973 oil crisis . The act split the Atomic Energy Commission into two new agencies: the Nuclear Regulatory Commission would regulate the commercial nuclear power industry, while the ERDA would manage the energy research and development , nuclear weapons , and naval reactors programs. [2] President Harry S. Truman signed the McMahon/Atomic Energy Act on August 1, 1946, transferring the control of atomic energy from military to civilian hands, effective on January 1, 1947. This shift gave the members of the AEC complete control of the plants, laboratories, equipment, and personnel assembled during the war to produce the atomic bomb. An increasing number of critics during the 1960s charged that the AEC's regulations were insufficiently rigorous in several important areas, including radiation protection standards, nuclear reactor safety, plant siting, and environmental protection. By 1974, the AEC's regulatory programs had come under such strong attack that the U.S. Congress decided to abolish the AEC. The AEC was abolished by the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974 , which assigned its functions to two new agencies: the Energy Research and Development Administration and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission . [5] On August 4, 1977, President Jimmy Carter signed into law the Department of Energy Organization Act of 1977, which created the Department of Energy . After the end of the Cold War , the department's attention also turned toward radioactive waste disposal and the maintenance of environmental quality . Commercial corporations can take many forms, including statutory corporations , corporations sole , joint-stock companies , cooperatives and others. The term is also part of the expression municipal corporation used only in formal contexts to refer to local governing bodies, although these are not commercial entities. Corporate may refer to either A corporation , a type of legal entity, often formed to conduct business Corporate (2006 film) , a 2006 Bollywood film starring Bipasha Basu Corporate (2017 film) , a 2017 French film Corporate (TV series) , a 2018 American comedy series A corporation is an organization—usually a group of people or a company —authorized by the state to act as a single entity (a legal entity recognized by private and public law "born out of statute"; a legal person in legal context) and recognized as such in law for certain purposes. 10 Early incorporated entities were established by charter (i.e., by an ad hoc act granted by a monarch or passed by a parliament or legislature). Most jurisdictions now allow the creation of new corporations through registration . Corporations come in many different types but are usually divided by the law of the jurisdiction where they are chartered based on two aspects: by whether they can issue stock , or by whether they are formed to make a profit . Depending on the number of owners, a corporation can be classified as aggregate (the subject of this article) or sole (a legal entity consisting of a single incorporated office occupied by a single natural person ). One of the most attractive early advantages business corporations offered to their investors, compared to earlier business entities like sole proprietorships and joint partnerships , was limited liability. [ clarification needed ] Limited liability means that a passive shareholder in a corporation will not be personally liable either for contractually agreed obligations of the corporation, or for torts (involuntary harms) committed by the corporation against a third party. Limited liability in contract is uncontroversial because the parties to the contract could have agreed to it and could agree to waive it by contract. However, limited liability in tort remains controversial because third parties do not agree to waive the right to pursue shareholders. There is significant evidence that limited liability in tort may lead to excessive corporate risk taking and more harm by corporations to third parties. Where local law distinguishes corporations by their ability to issue stock , corporations allowed to do so are referred to as stock corporations; one type of investment in the corporation is through stock, and owners of stock are referred to as stockholders or shareholders . Corporations not allowed to issue stock are referred to as non-stock corporations; i.e. those who are considered the owners of a non-stock corporation are persons (or other entities) who have obtained membership in the corporation and are referred to as a member of the corporation. Corporations chartered in regions where they are distinguished by whether they are allowed to be for-profit are referred to as for-profit and not-for-profit corporations, respectively. There is some overlap between stock/non-stock and for-profit/ not-for-profit in that not-for-profit corporations are nearly always non-stock as well. A for-profit corporation is almost always a stock corporation, but some for-profit corporations may choose to be non-stock. To simplify the explanation, whenever "stockholder" or "shareholder" is used in the rest of this article to refer to a stock corporation, it is presumed to mean the same as "member" for a non-profit corporation or for a profit, non-stock corporation. Registered corporations have legal personality recognized by local authorities and their shares are owned by shareholders whose liability is generally limited to their investment. Shareholders do not typically actively manage a corporation; shareholders instead elect or appoint a board of directors to control the corporation in a fiduciary capacity. In most circumstances, a shareholder may also serve as a director or officer of a corporation. Countries with co-determination employ the practice of workers of an enterprise having the right to vote for representatives on the board of directors in a company. In American English , the word corporation is most often used to describe large business corporations . In British English and in the Commonwealth countries , the term company is more widely used to describe the same sort of entity while the word corporation encompasses all incorporated entities. In American English, the word company can include entities such as partnerships that would not be referred to as companies in British English as they are not a separate legal entity . Late in the 19th century, a new form of the company having the limited liability protections of a corporation, and the more favorable tax treatment of either a sole proprietorship or partnership was developed. While not a corporation, this new type of entity became very attractive as an alternative for corporations not needing to issue stock. In Germany, the organization was referred to as Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung or GmbH. In the last quarter of the 20th century, this new form of non-corporate organization became available in the United States and other countries, and was known as the limited liability company or LLC. Since the GmbH and LLC forms of organization are technically not corporations (even though they have many of the same features), they will not be discussed in this article

Small business Small business - Wikipedia https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d7/Small_Businesses_-_geograph.org.uk_-_682645.jpg Small businesses are types of corporations , partnerships , or sole proprietorships which have a small number of employees and/or less annual revenue than a regular-sized business or corporation. Businesses are defined as "small" in terms of being able to apply for government support and qualify for preferential tax policy. The qualifications vary depending on the country and industry. Small businesses range from fifteen employees under the Australian Fair Work Act 2009 , fifty employees according to the definition used by the European Union , and fewer than five hundred employees to qualify for many U.S. Small Business Administration programs. While small businesses can also be classified according to other methods, such as annual revenues, shipments, sales, assets, annual gross, net revenue, net profits, the number of employees is one of the most widely used measures. Small businesses in many countries include service or retail operations such as convenience stores , small grocery stores , bakeries or delicatessens , hairdressers or tradespeople (e.g., carpenters , electricians ), restaurants , motels , photographers , very small-scale manufacturing, and Internet-related businesses such as web design and computer programming . Some professionals operate as small businesses, such as lawyers , accountants , dentists , medical doctors and developers (although these professionals can also work for large organizations or companies). Small businesses vary a great deal in terms of size, revenues, and regulatory authorization, both within a country and from country to country. Some small businesses, such as a home accounting business, may only require a business license. On the other hand, other small businesses, such as day cares , retirement homes , and restaurants serving liquor are more heavily regulated and may require inspection and certification from various government authorities.

Entrepreneurship Entrepreneurship - Wikipedia https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Dollar_sign_capitalism_logo.svg/800px-Dollar_sign_capitalism_logo.svg.png Entrepreneurship is the creation or extraction of economic value . With this definition, entrepreneurship is viewed as change, generally entailing risk beyond what is normally encountered in starting a business, which may include other values than simply economic ones. An entrepreneur is an individual who creates and/or invests in one or more businesses, bearing most of the risks and enjoying most of the rewards. The process of setting up a business is known as entrepreneurship. The entrepreneur is commonly seen as an innovator, a source of new ideas, goods, services, and business/or procedures. More narrow definitions have described entrepreneurship as the process of designing, launching and running a new business , which is often similar to a small business , or as the "capacity and willingness to develop, organize and manage a business venture along with any of its risks to make a profit . The people who create these businesses are often referred to as entrepreneurs. While definitions of entrepreneurship typically focus on the launching and running of businesses, due to the high risks involved in launching a start-up , a significant proportion of start-up businesses have to close due to "lack of funding, bad business decisions, government policies, an economic crisis, lack of market demand, or a combination of all of these. In the field of economics , the term entrepreneur is used for an entity which has the ability to translate inventions or technologies into products and services. In this sense, entrepreneurship describes activities on the part of both established firms and new businesses.

Small Business Administration - Wikipedia The United States Small Business Administration (SBA) is an independent agency of the United States government that provides support to entrepreneurs and small businesses. The mission of the Small Business Administration is "to maintain and strengthen the nation's economy by enabling the establishment and viability of small businesses and by assisting in the economic recovery of communities after disasters". The agency's activities have been summarized as the "3 Cs" of capital, contracts and counseling. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Business_Administration

Kamala Devi Harris- 49th Current Vice President of the United States Executive branch https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Kamala_Harris_Vice_Presidential_Portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/800px-Kamala_Harris_Vice_Presidential_Portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg Kamala Devi Harris ( born October 20, 1964) is an American politician and attorney who is the 49th and current vice president of the United States . She is the first female vice president and the highest-ranking female official in U.S. history, as well as the first African-American and first Asian-American vice president. A member of the Democratic Party , she previously served as the attorney general of California from 2011 to 2017 and as a United States senator representing California from 2017 to 2021. Born in Oakland , California, Harris graduated from Howard University and the University of California, Hastings College of the Law . She began her career in the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, before being recruited to the San Francisco District Attorney's Office and later the City Attorney of San Francisco 's office. In 2003, she was elected district attorney of San Francisco. She was elected Attorney General of California in 2010 and re-elected in 2014 . Harris served as the junior United States senator from California from 2017 to 2021; she defeated Loretta Sanchez in the 2016 Senate election to become the second African-American woman and the first South Asian American to serve in the United States Senate. As a senator, she advocated for healthcare reform, federal de-scheduling of cannabis , a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants, the DREAM Act , a ban on assault weapons , and progressive tax reform. She gained a national profile for her pointed questioning of Trump administration officials during Senate hearings, including Trump's second Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh , who was accused of sexual assault . Harris sought the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination , but withdrew from the race prior to the primaries . Joe Biden selected her as his running mate , and their ticket went on to defeat the incumbent president, Donald Trump , and vice president, Mike Pence , in the 2020 election . Harris became vice president upon being inaugurated on January 20, 2021, alongside President Joe Biden . Melvin Cordell Alma Gamble Amber Hawkins Charity Spencer Ethel Grant Sabrina Giesler

Comcast RISE Grant Website: https://utah.comcast.com/ (Check the news or business section for the grant announcement). Deadline: The application window for the Wasatch Front region is in September 2025 . Summary: This program provides a $5,000 monetary grant plus technology makeovers, marketing services, and business consultation. 3 It's an excellent opportunity for a business with a technology focus. Summary: If you are a woman-owned business, this grant is a great starting point, awarding $10,000 each month to a new winner. 4 Licenses and Certifications While there are no specific licenses to be a "compliance consultant" in Utah, you will need to operate a legal business and acquire industry-specific credentials. Business Registration: You must register your business with the Utah Department of Commerce and the Salt Lake City Business Licensing Division . 5 Professional Certifications: Your credibility hinges on your certifications. Consider these: Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP): A widely recognized certification for compliance professionals. Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA): If you focus on IT compliance. Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE): If you focus on financial compliance. Associations to Belong To Utah Compliance Association: This local association is a great place to network with other compliance professionals and potential clients. Salt Lake Chamber of Commerce: A crucial resource for networking, finding local business resources, and building relationships. Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE): A leading global organization for anti-fraud professionals, with local chapters for networking. The Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE): A national organization that provides certification, training, and a strong network. Steps to Expand the Business Define Your Niche: Instead of being a general compliance consultant, specialize in a specific area like cybersecurity compliance (e.g., NIST, CMMC) or financial compliance (e.g., SOX, GDPR). Build a Strong Online Presence: Your website is your storefront. Showcase your certifications, expertise, and client testimonials with clear pricing and service packages. Network Strategically: Attend events hosted by local chambers, industry associations, and legal or finance groups. Partner with law firms or accounting firms that may need to refer clients for compliance services. Content Marketing: Publish articles or create webinars on common compliance issues. This establishes you as a subject matter expert and drives traffic to your business. Government and Private Entities for Funding Utah Small Business Credit Initiative (USBCI): This program partners with local lenders to provide access to capital for small businesses. 6 While it's a loan program, it can be a flexible source of funding for working capital. Website: https://business.utah.gov/usbci/ U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA): The SBA offers various loan programs, not grants, but they are a primary source of capital for small businesses. Utah Microloan Fund: Provides loans up to $50,000 and free business advising for entrepreneurs who may not qualify for traditional bank loans. 7 SCORE: Provides free business mentorship from experienced professionals. Upcoming Conferences INTERFACE Salt Lake City: This event is scheduled for September 18, 2025 . 8 It's a great opportunity to network with IT and security professionals, a key market for your business. Finance and Business Networking - Salt Lake City: This networking event on September 24, 2025 , is a great place to meet accountants, bankers, and other professionals who could be clients or referral partners. There was additionally a request for the same info for real estate Grant funding in Pennsylvania and California. The information is posted below. It's the same general principle as in Georgia: direct grants specifically for starting a private lending and investing real estate business in Pennsylvania or California are highly unlikely. These activities are capital-driven and don't typically align with the objectives of most small business grants. However, here's how the landscape looks in Pennsylvania and California, with a focus on potentially relevant resources: Pennsylvania Likely Funding Sources (Not Grants Primarily): Small Business Administration (SBA) Loan Programs: Explore SBA-backed loans for operational costs and infrastructure. Website: https://www.sba.gov/ Pennsylvania Department of Community & Economic Development (DCED): While primarily focused on broader economic development, explore their funding programs for any general business assistance that might apply to your startup phase. Look for loan programs or initiatives supporting new businesses. Website: https://dced.pa.gov/programs-funding/ Local Economic Development Agencies and Initiatives: Check with economic development organizations in specific regions or cities within Pennsylvania where you plan to operate. They might have local loan programs or incentives. Financial Institutions: Building relationships with banks and credit unions is crucial for your own capital and potential partnerships. Private Investors/Partnerships: Raising capital for your lending pool will be the primary focus. Key Resources and Considerations (Pennsylvania): Pennsylvania Department of Banking and Securities: Understand the regulations for private lending in Pennsylvania. Website: https://www.dobs.pa.gov/ Real Estate Investor Associations in Pennsylvania: Network with other professionals. Examples include: Philadelphia Real Estate Investors Association (PhREIA): https://phreia.com/ Central PA Real Estate Investors Association (CPREIA): (Check for their online presence) Pennsylvania Small Business Development Centers (SBDC): Get business consulting and guidance. Website: https://pasbdc.org/ SCORE Chapters in Pennsylvania: Access free business mentoring. Website: https://www.score.org/find-mentor California Likely Funding Sources (Not Grants Primarily): Small Business Administration (SBA) Loan Programs: Explore SBA-backed loans. Website: https://www.sba.gov/ California Infrastructure and Economic Development Bank (IBank): Offers loan guarantee programs and some direct loan options for small businesses that might help with operational costs. Website: https://ibank.ca.gov/ California Office of the Small Business Advocate (CalOSBA): While their Dream Fund grant program was a one-time initiative, they provide resources and information on various funding options. Website: https://calosba.ca.gov/ Financial Institutions: Essential for your own capital and network. Private Investors/Partnerships: Crucial for funding your lending activities. Key Resources and Considerations (California): California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation (DFPI): Understand regulations for private lending. Website: https://dfpi.ca.gov/ Real Estate Investor Associations in California: Network with peers. Examples include: California Real Estate Investors Association (CalREIA): (Check for their online presence) Numerous local REIA groups throughout California (e.g., in Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego). California Small Business Development Center (SBDC): Get business consulting. Website: https://californiasbdc.org/ SCORE Chapters in California: Access free mentoring. Website: https://www.score.org/find-mentor General Advice for Pennsylvania and California (and Georgia): Focus on Building Capital: Your primary challenge will be securing the funds you need to lend and invest. Networking is Key: Connect with real estate professionals, investors, and potential borrowers. Demonstrate Expertise and Trust: Build a reputation for sound financial judgment and ethical practices. Compliance is Critical: Adhere strictly to all state and federal regulations. In summary, while direct grants for starting a private lending and investing real estate business in Pennsylvania or California are unlikely, focus on SBA loan programs, state-level business resources (primarily loan-focused in this sector), building relationships with financial institutions and private investors, and thoroughly understanding the regulatory environment in each state.

While grants specifically targeted towards starting a private lending and investing real estate business in Georgia are rare, here's a breakdown of potential avenues and resources: Understanding the Landscape Focus on Lending/Investing: Private lending and investing in real estate are capital-intensive activities. Traditional small business grants often favor businesses with job creation or specific social missions, which might not directly align with the core function of private lending/investing. Regulatory Environment: Private lending in real estate is subject to state and federal regulations. 1 Understanding these is crucial. Potential Funding and Resources (Less Likely to be Grants): Small Business Administration (SBA) Loan Programs: While not grants, SBA-backed loans could potentially provide capital for operational costs, marketing, or establishing your business infrastructure. 2 Explore the 7(a) loan program. Website: https://www.sba.gov/ Local and State Economic Development Programs: Some Georgia counties or cities might offer general small business incentives or loan programs that your business could potentially qualify for, even if not specific to real estate lending. Check with your local Chamber of Commerce or economic development authorities. Financial Institutions: Building relationships with banks and credit unions will be essential for your own funding and potentially for referrals or partnerships. Private Investors/Partnerships: Raising capital for your lending pool will likely involve attracting private investors or forming partnerships. Key Resources and Considerations: Licenses and Regulations: Understand the specific requirements for private lending and investing in real estate in Georgia. Consult with legal professionals specializing in this area. The Georgia Department of Banking and Finance is a key resource. Website: https://dbf.georgia.gov/ Niches and Other Markets: Hard money lending (short-term, asset-based loans). Fix-and-flip financing. Bridge loans. Development financing. Distressed property investment. Real estate crowdfunding platforms (as a sponsor or manager). Small Business Certifications: While not industry-specific for lending/investing, certifications in finance, business management, or real estate could enhance your credibility. Resources for Materials and Equipment: This would primarily involve office equipment, software for loan management and analysis, and marketing materials. Other Markets to Target: Real estate developers. Property flippers. Investors seeking alternative financing. Industries and Associations: Georgia Real Estate Investors Association (GaREIA): Provides networking and educational opportunities. 3 Website: https://gareia.com/ Atlanta Real Estate Investors Alliance (Atlanta REIA): Another active local association. Website: https://atlantareia.com/ American Association of Private Lenders (AAPL): A national organization for private lenders. Website: https://aaplonline.com/ Steps to Set Up at Home: Dedicated home office space. Secure and reliable computer systems and software for financial analysis, loan tracking, and communication. Professional website and online presence. Establish legal and accounting frameworks. Steps to Expand: Increase your lending capital. Expand your network of borrowers and investors. Offer a wider range of financing products. Hire staff to manage loan origination, underwriting, and servicing. Explore different geographic markets within Georgia or beyond. Governmental and Private Resources: Georgia Small Business Development Center (SBDC): Offers business consulting. 4 Website: https://www.georgiasbdc.org/ SCORE Mentors Atlanta: Provides free business mentoring. 5 Website: https://atlanta.score.org/ Obtaining Sponsorships: This is less common for financial businesses like private lending. However, you might explore sponsorships of real estate investor association events or local real estate meetups to increase visibility. Focus for Your Business: Given the nature of private lending and investing, your primary focus will be on: Building Capital: Attracting investors and managing your funds effectively. Networking: Connecting with borrowers and other real estate professionals. 6 Expertise: Demonstrating your knowledge of the market and your ability to assess risk. Compliance: Adhering to all relevant legal and financial regulations. While direct grants to start this type of business are unlikely, thoroughly researching the resources above for potential loan programs and focusing on building a strong, well-capitalized business with a solid network will be key to your success in the Georgia private lending and investing market.
